To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ureteral re-implantation is a safe and effective procedure for the treatment of VUR in children with a high rate of resolution of VUR.

the incidence of vesicoureteric reflux is 1 in 200 children, that it is more common in females, that it is bilateral in 30% of patients, that it is associated with urinary tract infection in 30% to 50% of cases, and that the risk of renal scarring is 10 to 30%.

the development and evaluation of an instrument to measure the quality of life in patients who have undergone surgery for vesicoureteric reflux.
the analysis and design of the control systems of the robot.
the study of the effect of ureteral re-implantation in children on the urinary tract and the kidney.
